tasks.short: Log call notes, promises to pay and debtor status in AFAS and the collections Excel.

today.trigger: After every call, mail or payment promise, and before the weekly debtor meeting with the Controller.
steps: Open the debtor in AFAS Profit and read the open items
Type a call or mail summary into the AFAS debtor notes
Update the promise-to-pay date and amount in the collections Excel
Mark disputes and who in operations is looking at them
Copy key figures into the weekly overview for the Controller
drudgery: Retyping the same facts in AFAS and Excel
Writing up phone calls from memory at the end of the day
Chasing colleagues for dispute status to record it
today.time_sinks: Double entry between AFAS and Excel and reconstructing calls afterwards; notes are uneven, so the next person re-reads whole mail threads.

lenses.faster: Teams call transcripts and Outlook threads are turned into a short structured note (reason, promise, date, amount, next step) that the officer confirms in one click.
lenses.autonomous: Payments, promise dates passing and dispute status changes update the debtor record by themselves; the officer only sees broken promises.
lenses.ambitious: A complete, consistent history per shipper for the first time, so the Controller and sales see why money is late, not only that it is.
lenses.joy: No more end-of-day typing from memory; the officer keeps the conversation and drops the paperwork.
lenses.options: The note generator proposes two or three readings of an ambiguous promise ('end of month' vs a fixed date) and asks which one to record.
lenses.altitude: The officer designs the note template and the dispute reason codes that feed the order-to-cash reports.
reach: Bookkeeper: keeping debtor master data and notes current
FP&A Analyst: cash-in forecast inputs from promise-to-pay data

tasks.human_edge: Judging what a customer really meant and how much a promise is worth, and deciding what belongs in the file for a later legal step.
tasks.pattern_why: Most recording is structured status that rules can update from AFAS and bank data; an llm_step only turns call transcripts and mails into the fixed note fields.

in_practice.trigger: Call ends in Teams, a debtor mail arrives, a payment posts or a promise date passes.
steps: Pull transcript or mail thread linked to the debtor number
LLM step fills note fields: reason, promise date, amount, contact, next action
Officer confirms or edits the note in a side panel
Write the note and promise to AFAS Profit via its connector
Rules flag broken promises and stale disputes to the officer's work list
in_practice.human_gate: Officer confirms each generated note before it is saved; automatic status updates from payments need no approval.
data_needed: AFAS open items and debtor notes
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS Profit debtor notes with source link and author, plus a change log table in SharePoint

evidence.claim: 30% of Dutch finance and credit professionals name manual work in Excel, mail and exports as the biggest cash-flow problem.
Microsoft Teams produces meeting transcripts and Copilot summaries that can feed structured notes.
Early file errors (wrong first letter, wrong interest or costs) only surface in court, so complete records matter.

risks: Recording calls with debtor contacts needs a legal basis and notice under AVG/GDPR
Summary misstates a promise and later weakens a claim
Works council may ask whether transcripts are used to assess the officer
research_questions: Does AFAS Profit's connector allow writing debtor notes and promise fields programmatically?
Will Noordhaven's customers accept a recording notice on collection calls?
How often do generated notes need correction in a four-week pilot?

tasks.short: Run the AFAS ageing list each morning and decide which overdue shippers to chase first.

today.trigger: Every morning and after each bank statement import.
steps: Export the AFAS ageing report to Excel
Filter overdue items above a threshold
Cross-check disputes and promises in the collections sheet
Sort by amount and age into a call list
Check Power BI for customers near their credit limit
drudgery: Daily export and re-filter of the same report
Manually removing items already paid or disputed
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding the priority list by hand daily; Power BI is a night behind, so same-day payments are missed.

lenses.faster: A rules-based priority list built from AFAS after each bank import replaces the Excel export and filter.
lenses.autonomous: The list rebuilds itself after every bank statement import and flags new overdue items, broken promises and limit breaches.
lenses.ambitious: Monitor every shipper's payment behaviour trend, not only the overdue top 20, and warn sales before a customer slips.
lenses.joy: The officer starts the day with a ranked list and context instead of an hour of spreadsheet work.
lenses.options: Show the same list ranked by amount, by risk of loss and by DSO impact, so the officer picks the day's strategy.
lenses.altitude: The officer owns the prioritisation rules and thresholds and reviews them monthly with the Controller.
reach: FP&A Analyst: weekly cash-in forecast from expected payment dates
Controller: DSO reporting for month close

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which customer relationship, seasonal pattern or dispute makes a 'red' item safe or a 'green' item dangerous.
tasks.pattern_why: Ageing, thresholds and ranking are clear rules on structured AFAS data; output is checkable.

in_practice.trigger: Bank statement import into AFAS completes, or 07:00 daily.
steps: Read open items, promises and disputes from AFAS
Apply ranking rules (age, amount, broken promise, credit limit)
Publish the work list to Power BI or a Teams tab
Alert the officer to new breaches above threshold
in_practice.human_gate: None for the list; the officer handles exceptions and changes rules with Controller sign-off.
data_needed: AFAS open items and due dates
in_practice.logs_to: Daily snapshot table of the priority list in the Power BI dataset

evidence.claim: 81% of Dutch finance professionals explain DSO after the fact; half plan cash-in at most two weeks ahead.
Credit management software builds prioritised collector work lists from ERP data.

risks: Rules tuned on amount alone hide small but chronic late payers
Stale nightly extract if the list is built in Power BI only
research_questions: Can AFAS data be read intra-day, or only via the nightly extract?
Which ranking rule best predicts which items actually get paid after a call?
How many overdue shippers are there on an average day?

tasks.short: Send reminders and first notices, and phone shippers who stay overdue.

today.trigger: Invoices pass their due date; weekly reminder run.
steps: Run the AFAS reminder (aanmaning) run
Check the batch for disputed or already paid items
Adjust wording for key accounts by hand in Word or Outlook
Phone overdue debtors from the priority list
Record the outcome
drudgery: Pulling disputed items out of the batch by hand
Rewriting the same reminder text for big customers
Finding the right contact person at the shipper
today.time_sinks: Cleaning the reminder batch and personalising letters; calls to wrong or outdated contacts.

lenses.faster: The reminder sequence runs from AFAS with disputed and promised items excluded automatically, and an LLM step adapts tone and language (Dutch, English, German) per customer.
lenses.autonomous: Standard first and second reminders go out on the due-date trigger without the officer; only key accounts and final notices wait for approval.
lenses.ambitious: Every overdue invoice gets a timely, correct reminder, with statutory commercial interest and the EUR 40 compensation stated correctly in the final notice.
lenses.joy: No more batch cleaning; the officer's phone time goes to the few customers where a call changes the outcome.
lenses.options: Draft three versions of a final notice (firm, relationship-preserving, with payment plan offer) for the officer to choose.
lenses.altitude: The officer designs the reminder sequence per customer segment and measures which step gets paid.
reach: Bookkeeper (AR): reminder runs
Sales account managers: first friendly nudge for key accounts

tasks.human_edge: The phone call: reading the customer, choosing when to push and when to protect a long relationship.
tasks.pattern_why: Dunning timing and exclusions are rules; an llm_step only varies wording inside approved templates.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice passes due date plus grace days per segment.
steps: Select overdue items, excluding disputes and active promises
Pick the sequence step and approved template
LLM step adapts wording and language within template limits
Send standard reminders from AFAS or Outlook; queue final notices and key accounts for approval
Create call tasks for items past the last written step
in_practice.human_gate: Officer approves final notices, key-account mails and anything stating interest or costs before it is sent.
data_needed: Contact persons and language per debtor
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS debtor reminder history and the sent-items mailbox

evidence.claim: Statutory commercial interest runs from the agreed due date (or 30 days after invoice) and at least EUR 40 compensation is due without a reminder.
Errors in the first letter, interest or costs surface later in court.
AFAS Profit has a built-in reminder (aanmaning) run.

risks: Reminder sent on a disputed invoice damages a key account
Wrong interest or cost figures weaken a later claim
Generated text drifts from approved legal wording
research_questions: What share of reminders today go out on items that were already disputed or paid?
Do reminders in the customer's own language get paid faster?
Does the legal adviser approve fixed template blocks for interest and costs?

tasks.short: Answer shippers' questions about their account: statements, invoice copies, proof of delivery, surcharges.

today.trigger: Mail or call from a customer's accounts payable team.
steps: Read the question in the shared debtor mailbox
Look up the invoice and open items in AFAS
Ask operations for proof of delivery or CMR
Compile statement or copies and reply
Log the question and any dispute
drudgery: Sending the same statement and invoice copies again
Waiting on depots for proof of delivery
today.time_sinks: Hunting for delivery documents at Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo and repeated simple statement requests.

lenses.faster: An agent classifies the mail, pulls the statement, invoice copy and proof of delivery, and drafts the reply.
lenses.autonomous: Requests for statements and invoice copies are answered on arrival; real complaints about rates or damage go to the officer.
lenses.ambitious: Every customer question answered the same day, and dispute causes counted so sales and operations can fix them at the source.
lenses.joy: The officer stops being a copy service and handles the questions that need thought.
lenses.options: For a disputed surcharge, the agent shows the contract clause, the rate card and two possible replies.
lenses.altitude: The officer owns the answer templates, the routing rules and the dispute reason feedback to sales and operations.
reach: Bookkeeper (AR): statement and copy requests
Customer service at sites: proof-of-delivery requests

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a complaint is justified and what Noordhaven concedes.
tasks.pattern_why: Several lookups across AFAS, SharePoint and operations, with exceptions; a person approves replies that admit or reject anything.

in_practice.trigger: Mail arrives in the debtor mailbox.
steps: Classify: statement, copy, proof of delivery, rate query, damage, other
Fetch documents from AFAS and the delivery archive
Draft reply with attachments
Send routine statement and copy requests after a rule check; queue the rest for approval
Log the question type and any dispute code in AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Officer approves every reply that touches rates, damage, credit notes or disputes; routine document sends are released by rule after a pilot.
data_needed: Proof of delivery and CMR archive
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS debtor notes and a question-type log in SharePoint for monthly dispute reporting

evidence.claim: Genpact's AR suite targets 30% faster dispute handling, as an indicative estimate with people on validation.
LLM-based mail triage and drafting in Outlook is available via Microsoft 365 Copilot.

risks: Documents sent to the wrong customer contact (AVG data breach)
Agent concedes a point in a draft that the officer misses
Proof of delivery not digitised at all sites
research_questions: What share of debtor mails are plain statement or copy requests?
Are proof-of-delivery documents digitally reachable for all three sites?
What are the top five dispute causes by value?

tasks.short: Talk late payers into paying, agree payment plans, settle damage claims against invoices.

today.trigger: Overdue item past written reminders or a customer contests payment.
steps: Read the account history and dispute file
Gather delivery proof, damage reports and contract terms
Call the customer and negotiate
Agree a plan or extension, get Controller approval if above limit
Confirm in writing and record
drudgery: Assembling the dispute file before each call
today.time_sinks: Preparation: finding the facts on damage claims and surcharges across operations and contracts.

lenses.faster: A one-page briefing per customer (history, dispute facts, contract terms, past promises) is ready before the call.
lenses.autonomous: Payment plan confirmations and instalment monitoring run by themselves once agreed.
lenses.ambitious: Every larger dispute prepared as if for court, with a clear settlement range agreed with the Controller in advance.
lenses.joy: Less digging, more of the conversation the officer is good at.
lenses.options: Three settlement scenarios with cash and margin effect: full payment, plan over three months, partial credit for damage.
lenses.altitude: The officer sets the negotiation rules: who may grant how long, which concessions, at which amounts.
reach: Sales account managers: commercial settlement of disputes
Controller: approval of small credit notes within agreed limits

tasks.human_edge: Persuasion, trust and judgement on what to concede; the officer carries the relationship and the decision.
tasks.pattern_why: The conversation and the decision stay with the person; AI prepares facts, options and follow-up.

in_practice.trigger: Item reaches the call stage or a dispute is logged.
steps: Copilot builds the briefing from AFAS, mail and the dispute file
It proposes settlement options within the approval matrix
Officer calls and negotiates
Copilot drafts the confirmation and sets up instalments in AFAS for approval
in_practice.human_gate: Officer decides in the call; plans and extensions above the matrix need Controller approval before confirmation.
data_needed: Approval matrix for plans and credit notes
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS debtor notes and a payment plan register in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Vendor suites keep people on validation and complex decisions in collections.
Dispute files in logistics turn on delivery proof, damage claims and surcharges.

risks: Over-reliance on a briefing that misses a side agreement made by sales
Creditworthiness scoring of sole-trader hauliers counts as high-risk AI under the EU AI Act (Annex III 5(b)) from 2 December 2027
research_questions: How much of a typical call's preparation time is document gathering?
Do briefed calls lead to more kept promises than unbriefed ones?
Which customers are natural persons (sole traders) and fall under AI Act duties?

tasks.short: Match incoming Rabobank payments to open invoices in AFAS and sort out the ones that don't match.

today.trigger: Daily Rabobank statement import into AFAS.
steps: Import the bank statement
Let AFAS auto-match on reference and amount
Work through unmatched lines by hand
Read remittance advice mails to split lump-sum payments
Post and clear items, park unknown receipts
drudgery: Splitting one payment over 40 invoices from a PDF remittance
Chasing customers for what a payment covers
today.time_sinks: Lump-sum payments without references and remittance advices in different formats per customer.

lenses.faster: AFAS matching rules run first; an LLM step reads remittance mails and PDFs and proposes the split for the rest.
lenses.autonomous: Proposals with exact totals and known invoice numbers post automatically; differences go to the officer.
lenses.ambitious: Cash posted same day every day, so DSO and the cash forecast are current during month close.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses typing invoice numbers from remittance PDFs.
lenses.options: For a short payment, show the likely explanations (deducted damage claim, discount taken, missing invoice) ranked.
lenses.altitude: The officer tunes the matching rules and remittance parsing, and tracks the touchless rate.
reach: Bookkeeper (AR): daily cash application
Accountant: suspense account clearing at month end

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what to do with short payments and unexplained deductions.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS rules handle structured matches; the remaining work is reading unstructured remittances into a checkable split whose total must equal the payment.

steps: AFAS auto-match on reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first sums
For unmatched lines, find remittance mail by payer and amount
LLM step extracts invoice numbers and amounts
Post automatically when totals and invoices match exactly; queue differences
in_practice.human_gate: Officer approves any split with a difference, deduction or unknown invoice.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS posting history with match method tag (rule, LLM, manual)

evidence.claim: AFAS matches bank lines on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first sums; misses go to a person.
Genpact expects up to 80% touchless cash application, stated as indicative.

risks: Wrong auto-post clears the wrong invoice and triggers a wrong reminder
Remittance formats change without notice
research_questions: What is today's AFAS auto-match rate on Noordhaven's statements?
What share of unmatched lines have a remittance mail?
How accurate is extraction on a sample of 200 past remittances?

tasks.short: Keep debtor master data right: address and contact changes, mergers, bankruptcies, closed companies.

today.trigger: Returned mail, customer notice, or a bankruptcy news item.
steps: Receive change notice by mail or from sales
Check the KvK register
Update the debtor in AFAS
Check the insolvency register for bankrupt debtors
Write off or file claims with the curator when needed
drudgery: Finding out too late that a customer went bankrupt
today.time_sinks: Ad hoc lookups and late discovery of insolvencies or dissolved companies.

lenses.faster: A scheduled check compares AFAS debtors to KvK and the insolvency register and proposes changes.
lenses.autonomous: Bankruptcies, dissolutions and address changes of debtors raise an alert and a draft change the same day.
lenses.ambitious: Clean master data across all debtors, so reminders and legal files never go to a wrong entity.
lenses.joy: No more manual register checks; the officer acts on alerts.
lenses.options: For a merger, propose either merging debtor accounts or keeping them apart, with effects on open items.
lenses.altitude: The officer defines the data quality rules for debtors and audits them monthly.
reach: Bookkeeper: debtor master data
Accountant: insolvency claims and write-off proposals

tasks.human_edge: Deciding on write-offs and insolvency claims, and spotting a debtor moving assets to a new entity.
tasks.pattern_why: Register comparisons on KvK numbers are rule-based and checkable.

in_practice.trigger: Weekly scheduled run, plus mail returned undeliverable.
steps: Pull KvK numbers of active debtors from AFAS
Query KvK API and insolvency register
Propose updates and flag insolvencies
Apply address changes automatically; queue insolvency actions
in_practice.human_gate: Officer approves entity changes, write-offs and claims to curators; address updates from KvK run automatically.

evidence.claim: KvK offers an API to the Handelsregister for company data lookups.
The Centraal Insolventieregister publishes Dutch insolvency rulings.

risks: Debtors without KvK numbers in AFAS
Data of sole traders is personal data under AVG
research_questions: What share of AFAS debtors have a valid KvK number?
How many insolvencies did Noordhaven learn of late in the past two years?
What does KvK API access cost per year?

tasks.short: Block credit, stop deliveries and hand unpaid files to the collection agency or lawyer.

steps: Propose a credit block to the Controller and inform sales
Consider holding goods in storage
Compile the file: invoices, contract, reminders, correspondence
Send it to the collection agency or lawyer
Notify the credit insurer where required
drudgery: Assembling the hand-over file document by document
today.time_sinks: Building complete files and coordinating with sales on whether to block a customer.

lenses.faster: An agent builds the hand-over file with interest and EUR 40 compensation calculated and all reminders attached.
lenses.autonomous: When the last step passes without payment, the file and block proposal are prepared without a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: Every file court-proof from the first letter, so fewer claims fail on form.
lenses.joy: The officer decides; the agent does the binder work.
lenses.options: Show choices side by side: extra call, payment plan, agency, lawyer, insurer claim, with cost and expected recovery.
lenses.altitude: The officer sets escalation criteria and checks agencies' registration and results.
reach: Controller: credit block decisions within limits
Accountant: provisions for doubtful debts

tasks.human_edge: Deciding to escalate and weighing the customer relationship against recovery.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across systems with judgement on exceptions; a person decides before anything leaves.

steps: Assemble invoices, contract, reminders and correspondence
Calculate statutory interest and compensation
Draft block proposal and hand-over letter
Check agency registration (Wki)
Queue for decision
in_practice.human_gate: Officer and Controller decide on block, escalation and insurer notice; nothing is sent before approval.
in_practice.logs_to: Escalation register in SharePoint and AFAS debtor notes

evidence.claim: Syncasso drafts a summons from a file in two minutes; handling time falls from 165 to 62 minutes, by the vendor's own figure.
Since 1 October 2026 no collection costs or further interest are owed if an unregistered party sends reminders for a natural-person debtor.
Commercial interest and EUR 40 minimum compensation rules.

risks: Unregistered agency costs collection fees for sole-trader debtors
Wrong calculation found only in court
A warehouse lien on goods depends on contract terms (E1)
research_questions: Are Noordhaven's agencies registered under the Wki?
How many files went to agencies last year and how many failed on form?
Do the warehouse terms allow holding goods for unpaid invoices?

role.altitude: From chasing invoices to running Noordhaven's order-to-cash rules: credit limits, reminder sequences, matching rules, escalation criteria, and dispute causes fed back to sales and operations, measured on DSO and share of invoices disputed.
reach: Bookkeeper (AR): cash application and reminder runs
FP&A Analyst: cash-in forecast from promise and payment data
Controller: DSO reporting and credit block decisions within limits
Sales account managers: dispute root-cause follow-up
role.ceiling_note: About half of the role's hours (monitoring, recording, posting, admin, reminders) can largely run as rules with an officer on exceptions; conversations, settlements and escalation decisions stay human, and AI Act duties on scoring sole-trader hauliers from December 2027 limit automated credit decisions.
skills_to_grow: Writing and testing business rules in AFAS and Power BI
Reviewing AI drafts against BW 6:119a and Wki rules
Dispute root-cause analysis with sales and operations
role.ambitious_version: The officer runs a near-touchless order-to-cash flow with same-day cash posting, a live cash-in forecast for FP&A, and a monthly dispute report that removes the top causes at the source, cutting DSO and making the month close faster.
